caveats.greek: STEPBible's TAGNT header says its variants include every variant in the major editions, and manuscript variants before AD 500 that are used by translators. It does not note insignificant differences (spelling, or word order that does not change the meaning).
caveats.hebrew: STEPBible's TAHOT header says the Qere/Ketiv readings and the restored and Greek-derived (X) words are recorded throughout, but that most other variants (Dead Sea Scrolls, Aleppo, Cairensis, Ben Chaim, BHS and so on) are yet to be added. No flag on a Hebrew word therefore does not prove that no variant exists.

greekNoteMarkers.^: Extra text: some manuscripts have text not found in others.
greekNoteMarkers.v: Variant: some manuscripts have significantly different wording.

greekNoteVocabulary: In the source's variant notes, readings translated by the KJV are called "traditional", readings that agree with NA27 are called "older", and others are called "a few".

greekOtherTokens.KJV: The KJV translators' text (where the KJV departs from the Textus Receptus)

greekTypeLetters.K: Greek used by the KJV translators, based on Scrivener 1894
greekTypeLetters.N: Greek in the Nestle-Aland editions, as used by most modern translators
greekTypeLetters.O: other Greek found in major editions but rarely translated

hebrewSourceShort.D: a Dead Sea or Judean Desert manuscript

hebrewSources.B: the Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia (BHS), where it deviates from the Masoretic text
hebrewSources.D: a Dead Sea or Judean Desert manuscript
hebrewSources.E: an emendation of ancient sources (a scholarly guess at the original when the Hebrew looks garbled)
hebrewSources.F: formatting the text differently (pointing or word divisions change, no letters change)
hebrewSources.H: the Ben Chaim edition (the Second Rabbinic Bible)
hebrewSources.K: the Ketiv (the uncorrected text, as written)
hebrewSources.P: alternate punctuation, as marked in major manuscripts
hebrewSources.Q: the Qere (the scribes' marginal correction, which translators normally follow)
hebrewSources.R: restored text based on Leningrad parallels (Jos 21:36-37 from 1Ch 6:63-64; Neh 7:67b from Ezr 2:66)
hebrewSources.S: Scribal traditions (Itture Sopherim, Tiqqune Sopherim, Masora and similar)
hebrewSources.V: a variant in some manuscripts other than those above
hebrewSources.X: extra words preserved in the Greek (LXX), converted back to Hebrew as in the apparatus of BHS or BHK
